trust_decision.summary: An OPA permission query decides, per project resource (/projects/<name>) and per action (create/update/delete), whether the caller's member ids from the auth session may write that project; at the pinned commit this decision is only made on read paths (GetAll, getProjectByName, export) and on no project write path at all, so any authenticated user can create/update/delete any project.

landing_point.why: The summary says project write paths lack authorization; the dashboard project resource is the first place to look, and there Update/deleteProject build PermissionOptions with only OverrideHeaderValue while the read paths in the same file (GetAll at project.go:87-90, getProjectByName at project.go:644-648) already pass MemberIds and RaiseForbidden.

fix_sites.entry_point: PUT /api/projects/{id} (ResourceMethodUpdate) and legacy PUT /api/projects -> updateProject -> Update
POST /api/projects, POST /api/projects?import=true, nuctl create project, nuctl import project
PUT /api/projects/{id}, legacy PUT /api/projects (both arrive via the dashboard resource)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The local platform is a single-user dev/CI backend chosen by platform.kind (pkg/platform/factory/factory.go:56-62), so a solver can argue its project write paths never face authenticated multi-user traffic, even though the same file enforces OPA for functions and function events (pkg/platform/local/platform.go:180-189, 416-424, 629-639).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Project read permissions are populated in OPA only AFTER the project exists (EnsureProjectRead is retried for 10s post-create), and the default OPA client is nop; an over-broad fix that reuses the read/EnsureProjectRead path at create time, or that forbids when MemberIds is empty, denies every first-time project creation and breaks the default no-OPA deployments and internal callers.

O6_input_shapes: update with the project name in the URL path (PUT /api/projects/{id}) vs in the request body or X-Nuclio-Project-Name header (legacy PUT /api/projects)
create with an explicit metadata.name vs the create-and-wait path used by project import
delete with the X-Nuclio-Delete-Project-Strategy header set to cascading, restricted, or unset (default restricted)
caller with a populated auth session vs nil/empty session (MemberIds resolves to an empty list)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: nuctl delete projects calls Platform.DeleteProject directly; the fix's new check is passed the caller's PermissionOptions and never forces RaiseForbidden, so a false verdict returns (false, nil) and the delete proceeds
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: nuctl is an operator CLI that runs with cluster credentials, not the multiuser dashboard access path
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: pkg/nuctl/command, two packages from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: nuctl create/import projects calls Platform.CreateProject with an empty PermissionOptions and no AuthSession, so the forced RaiseForbidden query has no member ids to authorize
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: project creation from a CLI is assumed to be an operator/admin action outside the per-user permission model
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: pkg/nuctl/command, two packages from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: dashboard POST /api/projects?import=true creates the missing project via CreateAndWait with PermissionOptions carrying only OverrideHeaderValue, so the platform-level create check runs with no member ids
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: import first calls GetProjects with RaiseForbidden, so the caller can argue the project-existence check already authorizes the write
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: another platform method that queries OPA but forgets to force RaiseForbidden so the verdict is discarded
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the surrounding platform methods in the same tree (kube/platform.go:1142-1152, 1181-1190) all copy the options and force RaiseForbidden, so a missing force looks like a deliberate pass-through.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a dashboard write route that hand-builds PermissionOptions instead of calling the existing newPermissionOptions helper, dropping MemberIds
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the helper already exists and is used by apigateway.go (five sites) and function.go:743, so an inlined struct with a missing field is an easy, plausible maintainer slip.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the same project write guard added to the local platform's CreateProject/UpdateProject/DeleteProject
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the file already performs OPA checks in exactly this style for functions, redeploy and function events, so a maintainer mirroring them onto projects is natural.

O9_family: missing authorization on write paths (CWE-862, broken access control / A01)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: add MemberIds and RaiseForbidden to the two dashboard PermissionOptions blocks (Update, deleteProject) and stop there, leaving the platform layer, the nuctl callers and the local platform untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: The leader/follower project-forwarding wrapper (pkg/platform/abstract/project/external/client.go:94-140) was read only to confirm those requests re-enter the same dashboard resource; nothing outside this advisory's project write protection was pursued.
